    41→/// The LRU Cache stores `PendingComponents`, which store block and its associated blob data:

    47→/// in `PendingComponents` is ~12.29 MB. Setting this to 32 means the maximum size of the cache is
    48→/// approximately 0.4 GB.

    50→/// `PendingComponents` are now never removed from the cache manually are only removed via LRU
    51→/// eviction to prevent race conditions (#7961), so we expect this cache to be full all the time.

    56→/// Cache to hold fully valid data that can't be imported to fork-choice yet. After Dencun hard-fork
    57→/// blocks have a sidecar of data that is received separately from the network. We call the concept
    58→/// of a block "becoming available" when all of its import dependencies are inserted into this
    59→/// cache.
    60→///
    61→/// Usually a block becomes available on its slot within a second of receiving its first component
    62→/// over gossip. However, a block may never become available if a malicious proposer does not
    63→/// publish its data, or there are network issues that prevent us from receiving it. If the block
    64→/// does not become available after some time we can safely forget about it. Consider these two
    65→/// cases:
    66→///
    67→/// - Global unavailability: If nobody has received the block components it's likely that the
    68→///   proposer never made the block available. So we can safely forget about the block as it will
    69→///   never become available.
    70→/// - Local unavailability: Some fraction of the network has received all block components, but not us.
    71→///   Some of our peers will eventually attest to a descendant of that block and lookup sync will
    72→///   fetch its components. Therefore it's not strictly necessary to hold to the partially available
    73→///   block for too long as we can recover from other peers.
    74→///
    75→/// Even in periods of non-finality, the proposer is expected to publish the block's data
    76→/// immediately. Because this cache only holds fully valid data, its capacity is bound to 1 block
    77→/// per slot and fork: before inserting into this cache we check the proposer signature and correct
    78→/// proposer. Having a capacity > 1 is an optimization to prevent sync lookup from having re-fetch
    79→/// data during moments of unstable network conditions.

    92→    Success(AvailabilityAndReconstructedColumns<E>),
    93→    NotStarted(&'static str),
    94→    RecoveredColumnsNotImported(&'static str),

   103→    Available(Box<AvailableExecutedBlock<E>>),

   452→

   469→                        block,
   470→                        blob_data: AvailableBlockData::DataColumns(

   473→                        blobs_available_timestamp: None,
   474→                        spec: self.spec.clone(),
   475→                    })
   476→                } else {
   477→                    MaybeAvailableBlock::AvailabilityPending { block_root, block }
   478→                }
   479→            } else {

   482→                    block,
   483→                    blob_data: AvailableBlockData::NoData,
   484→                    blobs_available_timestamp: None,
   485→                    spec: self.spec.clone(),
   486→                })
   487→            };

   550→    pub fn reconstruct_data_columns(
   551→        &self,
   552→        block_root: &Hash256,
   553→    ) -> Result<DataColumnReconstructionResult<T::EthSpec>, AvailabilityCheckError> {
   554→        let verified_data_columns = match self
   555→            .availability_cache
   556→            .check_and_set_reconstruction_started(block_root)
   557→        {
   558→            ReconstructColumnsDecision::Yes(verified_data_columns) => verified_data_columns,
   559→            ReconstructColumnsDecision::No(reason) => {
   560→                return Ok(DataColumnReconstructionResult::NotStarted(reason));
   561→            }
   562→        };
   563→
   564→        metrics::inc_counter(&KZG_DATA_COLUMN_RECONSTRUCTION_ATTEMPTS);
   565→        let timer = metrics::start_timer(&metrics::DATA_AVAILABILITY_RECONSTRUCTION_TIME);
   566→
   567→        let all_data_columns = KzgVerifiedCustodyDataColumn::reconstruct_columns(
   568→            &self.kzg,
   569→            &verified_data_columns,
   570→            &self.spec,
   571→        )
   572→        .map_err(|e| {
   573→            error!(
   574→                ?block_root,
   575→                error = ?e,
   576→                "Error reconstructing data columns"
   577→            );
   578→            self.availability_cache
   579→                .handle_reconstruction_failure(block_root);
   580→            metrics::inc_counter(&KZG_DATA_COLUMN_RECONSTRUCTION_FAILURES);
   581→            AvailabilityCheckError::ReconstructColumnsError(e)
   582→        })?;
   583→
   584→        // Check indices from cache again to make sure we don't publish components we've already received.
   585→        let Some(existing_column_indices) = self.cached_data_column_indexes(block_root) else {
   586→            return Err(AvailabilityCheckError::Unexpected(
   587→                "block no longer exists in the data availability checker".to_string(),
   588→            ));
   589→        };
   590→
   591→        let data_columns_to_publish = all_data_columns
   592→            .into_iter()
   593→            .filter(|d| !existing_column_indices.contains(&d.index()))
   594→            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
   595→
   596→        let Some(slot) = data_columns_to_publish
   597→            .first()
   598→            .map(|d| d.as_data_column().slot())
   599→        else {
   600→            return Ok(DataColumnReconstructionResult::RecoveredColumnsNotImported(
   601→                "No new columns to import and publish",
   602→            ));
   603→        };
   604→
   605→        metrics::stop_timer(timer);
   606→        metrics::inc_counter_by(
   607→            &metrics::DATA_AVAILABILITY_RECONSTRUCTED_COLUMNS,
   608→            data_columns_to_publish.len() as u64,
   609→        );
   610→
   611→        debug!(
   612→            count = data_columns_to_publish.len(),
   613→            ?block_root,
   614→            %slot,
   615→            "Reconstructed columns"
   616→        );
   617→
   618→        self.availability_cache
   619→            .put_kzg_verified_data_columns(*block_root, data_columns_to_publish.clone())
   620→            .map(|availability| {
   621→                DataColumnReconstructionResult::Success((
   622→                    availability,
   623→                    data_columns_to_publish
   624→                        .into_iter()
   625→                        .map(|d| d.clone_arc())
   626→                        .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
   627→                ))
   628→            })
   629→    }
   630→}

   638→pub fn start_availability_cache_maintenance_service<T: BeaconChainTypes>(
   639→    executor: TaskExecutor,
   640→    chain: Arc<BeaconChain<T>>,
   641→) {
   642→    // this cache only needs to be maintained if deneb is configured
   643→    if chain.spec.deneb_fork_epoch.is_some() {
   644→        let overflow_cache = chain.data_availability_checker.availability_cache.clone();
   645→        executor.spawn(
   646→            async move { availability_cache_maintenance_service(chain, overflow_cache).await },
   647→            "availability_cache_service",
   648→        );
   649→    } else {
   650→        debug!("Deneb fork not configured, not starting availability cache maintenance service");
   651→    }
   652→}
   653→
   654→async fn availability_cache_maintenance_service<T: BeaconChainTypes>(
   655→    chain: Arc<BeaconChain<T>>,
   656→    overflow_cache: Arc<DataAvailabilityCheckerInner<T>>,
   657→) {
   658→    let epoch_duration = chain.slot_clock.slot_duration() * T::EthSpec::slots_per_epoch() as u32;
   659→    loop {
   660→        match chain
   661→            .slot_clock
   662→            .duration_to_next_epoch(T::EthSpec::slots_per_epoch())
   663→        {
   664→            Some(duration) => {
   665→                // this service should run 3/4 of the way through the epoch
   666→                let additional_delay = (epoch_duration * 3) / 4;
   667→                tokio::time::sleep(duration + additional_delay).await;
   668→
   669→                let Some(deneb_fork_epoch) = chain.spec.deneb_fork_epoch else {
   670→                    // shutdown service if deneb fork epoch not set
   671→                    break;
   672→                };
   673→
   674→                debug!("Availability cache maintenance service firing");
   675→                let Some(current_epoch) = chain
   676→                    .slot_clock
   677→                    .now()
   678→                    .map(|slot| slot.epoch(T::EthSpec::slots_per_epoch()))
   679→                else {
   680→                    continue;
   681→                };
   682→
   683→                if current_epoch < deneb_fork_epoch {
   684→                    // we are not in deneb yet
   685→                    continue;
   686→                }
   687→
   688→                let finalized_epoch = chain
   689→                    .canonical_head
   690→                    .fork_choice_read_lock()
   691→                    .finalized_checkpoint()
   692→                    .epoch;
   693→
   694→                let Some(min_epochs_for_blobs) = chain
   695→                    .spec
   696→                    .min_epoch_data_availability_boundary(current_epoch)
   697→                else {
   698→                    // Shutdown service if deneb fork epoch not set. Unreachable as the same check is performed above.
   699→                    break;
   700→                };
   701→
   702→                // any data belonging to an epoch before this should be pruned
   703→                let cutoff_epoch = std::cmp::max(finalized_epoch + 1, min_epochs_for_blobs);
   704→
   705→                if let Err(e) = overflow_cache.do_maintenance(cutoff_epoch) {
   706→                    error!(error = ?e,"Failed to maintain availability cache");
   707→                }
   708→            }
   709→            None => {
   710→                error!("Failed to read slot clock");
   711→                // If we can't read the slot clock, just wait another slot.
   712→                tokio::time::sleep(chain.slot_clock.slot_duration()).await;
   713→            }
   714→        };
   715→    }
   716→}
